full_review:
Accept for the bounded purpose of independent, complete-available-text paper-reading review. I found no required scientific correction in the frozen reading.md or source.json. This is a manual independent reviewer response, not a protected runtime ReviewSession receipt, experiment-result verification, author implementation audit, or repository performance acceptance.

Identity and immutable inputs. I read the supplied manifest and independently recomputed SHA-256 for all nine references, including the actual HTML and complete extracted text. All match the frozen manifest. The manifest itself matches bc3dc8e814411068a76f58c25ce95c2520eb8e0bf42a6d93e3fe00cd21325098. The text is 69,349 Unicode characters (69,992 UTF-8 bytes), so source.json's character count is consistent rather than a byte-count claim. The observed primary artifact is MemSteer 2610.39276v1, with header date 29 Oct 2026. No network authenticity, external author repository, or current provider version is certified here.

Actual independent coverage. I read the complete actual paper.txt sequentially in ranges [0,18000), [18000,36000), [36000,54000), [54000,69349), rather than treating the producer summary or coverage flags as the paper. This covers the abstract, main sections 1–5 and all subsections, ethics/reproducibility/LLM-usage statements, complete reference list, Appendices A.1–A.5, B.1–B.5 and C, every cell in Tables 1–9 as exposed in the text, Figures 1–5 captions, numbered Equations 1–2 and the unnumbered definitions/evaluation and acceptance formulas. The HTML is hash-verified; I did not independently perform a full HTML visual audit, PDF rendering, image/pixel review, or curve-point extraction. The reading record accurately preserves those limits.

Method and scientific objects. Equation 1 defines history-derived (question, answer, source-record evidence) supervision with provenance spans, not parameter training. The paper distinguishes graph material preparation, an evidence-grounded answer plan, programmatic checks before a separate question call, source-grounded semantic audit, and blind answer recovery. The reading correctly describes exact type-normalized agreement and record-level citation coverage. It explicitly avoids the invalid inference that every cited record is necessary, that shared LLM errors are excluded, or that successful recovery from the sampled bundle proves retrieval from the entire history. Its interpretation of train/validation disjoint QA and possible common source history is appropriately limited.

Equation 2 and the design d=(storage,retrieval,context) are represented correctly. The report accurately distinguishes final-context sufficiency, missing evidence recoverable by source ID, and storage failures, while withholding a causal-completeness guarantee. It accurately gives strict binary validation-accuracy improvement, refresh of training failures after acceptance, and at-most-ten-per-category feedback under the context budget. Twenty reflective iterations repeatedly consult the same validation set, so the report correctly retains adaptive-selection risk. Fixed answering roles do not make different external optimizers' starting systems or search spaces controlled equivalents. The report correctly treats generated gold evidence as reference evidence rather than human certification.

Experiments, population and denominators. ATM has 11,034 records, 1,013 main evaluation questions and 31 Hard questions. ATM generated and Official conditions use 400 training plus 200 validation questions, while Official's 600 remain in the 1,013 evaluation population. RHELM has 21,142 interaction records and 1,305 official questions across ten personas; Official uses 524 training plus 264 validation, still in evaluation. The final generated configuration is described in the paper as 788 generated training items, with no separately sufficient final generated-validation count. The report correctly refuses to infer equal supervision budgets or a clean common unseen test set. Final QS, binary design selection, RHELM accuracy and evidence recall are separated. Reference leaderboard rows and different answerer backbones are not represented as a common locally rerun controlled experiment.

Primary numerical checks. Table 1's Base main QS54.9 to MemSteer68.3 is +13.4 percentage points, Hard8.2 to29.1 is +20.9; recall61.7 to84.1 and10.0 to43.6 is reported correctly. Official67.3/27.9 yields displayed QS differences1.0/1.2, whereas paper prose says1.1/1.3; the reading explicitly preserves this discrepancy without manufacturing unrounded values. It similarly preserves MemEvolve Hard's displayed 7.1 to9.5 versus the printed +2.3 arrow and the18.7 to18.6 recall decline. Table 2's generated26.4/39.9 improves Base22.3/33.3 by4.1/6.6 while remaining below Official26.5/40.7; the no-external RAG k50 value28.9 blocks a blanket best-system claim. Frozen ATM transfer26.4/38.6 and continuation30.6/42.8 are distinguished from direct Base optimization and additional optimization budget.

Negative results and selection. The reading does not hide Table 9(a)'s held-out pooled35.3 to35.1 or Martin41.2 to37.7, and correctly distinguishes source679, held-out626 and all1,305 evaluation questions. Personal continuation's Martin421=282+139 and David337=223+114 generated supervision and228/158 official evaluations are correct. All-persona improvement in Table9(b) is not mislabeled held-out transfer. Table8 fact59.4 to55.6 and mixed51.9 to51.4 regressions under continuation, and Qwen external15.3 to8.1 degradation, are retained. These are important boundaries on general transfer or longer-context claims.

Ablations and cost. Table4's four-criterion conjunctive binary QA score, two-judge mean, retention fractions21.2/42.1/47.9 and inconsistent downstream effects are correctly distinguished. Ragas checks lower Hard23.3 to20.7 despite improved main QS, and Naive54.2/5.3 underperforms Base54.9/8.2. Table5 holds the same600 tasks and stated generation conditions; quality67.8/73.1/85.9 and64.0k/68.2k/105.1k tokens per question are accurately reproduced. The separate common GPT4.1mini filter, blind GPT4.1 quality review of passing QA, and different Table4 evaluation setup are not collapsed into one human-truth metric or complete end-to-end bill. Full retries, optimization, API costs, wall clock and all-role user costs remain unknown. B.2 changes validation size along with the training budget and samples from an expanded generated pool; it is not an isolated training-size intervention. Figure3 conclusions are restricted to prose/caption, with no invented numerical bars. The nine accepted architecture revisions in B.5 are one trajectory, not nine independent component ablations. Table7 reruns the complete QA pipeline with the alternate judge and therefore is not an isolated rescore of identical responses; query variation and recall differences are explicitly retained.

Limitations and ethics. The report accurately carries the paper's un-certified LLM supervision/shared bias, history-question versus real-user-need mismatch, retrieval-centric search space, two-benchmark scope and synthetic RHELM personas. It preserves the third-party API privacy concern and remote API nondeterminism/provider-update caveat. The source metadata does not claim identified/pinned author code, read author data or replicated experiments. Textual identification of reference GitHub links is not escalated into an exhaustive external author-code search.

Repository applicability and historical boundaries. I read AGENTS, the project-document, knowledge-access, result-reuse and dual-main workflows, concise-engineering guidance and decision-gate material; read the entire guide directory readonly (GUIDE.md empty; README is directory governance, not substantive project authorization); read the complete frozen stable Plan63 prefix, relevant SYSTEM-99 index/detail context, the preceding curation report and recovery report. The suggested repository use is a future evaluation taxonomy distinguishing evidence retention, delivery and interpretation, with real end-task quality and complete costs still to validate. It does not authorize a new memory service, generated-code execution, embedding service, migration, new permission, or acceptance from synthetic QA. Existing MemoryLedger/reference contracts remain declared-dependency gates, not automatic hidden-dependency discovery.

The source's status_at_freeze pending/zero-new-credit is explicitly a historical freeze snapshot and is not a contradiction requiring source mutation after this review. The old curation paper's missing original feedback remains unknown/expired and zero-credit; I did not rerun or review it. Recovery's older three papers/six missing private originals remain missing. Windows, FD57, StageI, backend and all previously exhausted/frozen budgets remain unchanged. Historical source/report counts are not retroactively re-certified by this result. This paper may contribute at most one distinct completed reading after the parent records and publishes the bounded outcome; it does not close SYSTEM-99's real host, full inputs, terminal quality, all-role cost, concurrent recovery or complete uninstall-transaction gaps.

No required findings. Optional nonblocking follow-up: if these paper results are later used to design empirical acceptance, obtain a clearly separate untouched evaluation population, state actual generated RHELM validation count and all generation/selection costs, and preserve per-persona/category regressions. That is future experimental design, not a demand to speculate or edit this correctly limited frozen reading. No second reviewer call is needed for the current artifact. The sole original review was completed within the original deadline. No tests, models, probes, services, network calls, paid resources, publication or additional agents were used by this reviewer. Only the assigned review JSON is written; public packet and TASK remain the parent's responsibility.
